pr_title: Prevent PEJ on loading and on readonly replica.
pr_body:
Fix #11643

While Redis loading data from disk (AOF or RDB), modules will get key space notifications. In such stage the module should not register any PEJ, the main reason this is forbidden is that PEJ purpose is to perform a write operation as a reaction to the key space notification. Write operations should not be performed while loading data and so there is no reason to register a PEJ. 

Same argument also apply to readonly replica. module should not perform any writes as a reaction to key space notifications and so it should not register a PEJ.

If a module need to perform some other task which is not involve writing, he can do it on the key space notification callback itself.

issue_context.title: Issues with PostExecUnitJobs and AOF
issue_context.body:
# Intro

The main issue we have is that currently `call` is in charge of incr/decr of `server.in_nested_call` (soon to be `server.execution_nesting`) and that AOF calls to `proc` directly, and doesn't even call `afterCommand`.
The result is that while loading AOF, all the PEJs will be accumulated and will only be executed after the first non-AOF command

# Other issues
In addition to the above:
1. The is a difference between startup AOF and DEBUG LOADAOF: In the latter server.execution_nesting is 1 throughout the loading process, and in the former, it's 0. We need to see if it has any adverse effects.
2.  if we have MULTI/EXEC inside an AOF, PEJ will be executed after each command in the transaction (AOF calls `proc` but `execCommand` calls `call`, incrementing `execution_nesting` from 0 to 1 and then from 1 to 0 in `afterCommand`), breaking the contract of PEJs

# To do
* We need to define the desired behavior and to add more tests that handle PEJs, propagation, and AOF
* we need to decide if modules will be allowed to register PEJ from AOF loading, and from replicas.

trying to challenge this to be on the safe side:
what if the module wants to react to changes, and instead of propagating the reaction, it wants to perform a similar reaction in the replica?

e.g. on every key that's added, increment some counter.

well, if the counter is in the module's global memory (not part of the redis data set), then it can do that from the KSN, no need for PEJ.
but what if the counter is a key? it did have a PEJ in the master to increment that key, and it could have propagated that increment. but maybe for something more complicated than a counter, propagation is excessive and the module would rather compute it locally and modify the keyspace?

in theory, maybe we can match the client in the CTX to the master client, like what's done here:
```
    if (server.masterhost && server.repl_slave_ro &&
        !obey_client &&
        is_write_command)
```
calling @guybe7 and @yossigo to comment too.
@oranagra I agree with you about it, we need some good arguments about why no PEJ use case is applicable in these cases.

> in theory, maybe we can match the client in the CTX to the master client, like what's done here:

Then we also need to support PEJ on AOF because this logic effect will not be propagated to it. If the propagation is expensive then the module could have register a command that perform this logic and execute this command on the PEJ and replicate it as well. Complex propagation is not a good argument here in my opinion because it can be avoided easily.

yes, the `obey_client` part above also covers AOF.

i'm not certain about this use case. i'm was actually leaning towards accepting this change, just trying to have some argument to be sure one way or the other.

p.s. arguably by not blocking it, we leave it for the module's responsibility to check, and thus we allow more flexibility for odd use cases. but then we'll need to take care of the original issue and make sure to call afterCommand when processing AOF.

@oranagra yes this is what I meant, the `obey_client` will cover the registration part but we will need to cover the AOF issue and call the PEJ properly.
My opinion is that we should encourage an effect replication (which is what we will do if we forbid PEJ on replica and when loading).

discussed it with @guybe7.
initially i argued that if a module wants to implement something similar to a script, and do script replication (rather than effects replication), it'll need to do the same modifications it did on the master, on the replica as well.
but that's actually about module that implements commands, not one that listens on KSN of other commands.

so for KSN the reasoning is that module can listen on them to update it's global state (index / counters), and that's not considered a write from redis's point of view, but if it decides to write that data into a key (inside the PEJ), it should propagate that, and then it doesn't need, and shouldn't do the same on the replica / AOF loading.

not sure i managed to convey the entire discussion, @guybe7 feel free to elaborate, but the bottom line is that we agree with the current PR that wishes to block this.
